purpose: Train Doré aesthetic judgement and complete magazine layout design from issue-level evidence, not style imitation.

issues.editorial_problem: Make the magazine itself a working field for graphic culture rather than a neutral carrier.
cover: jacket-with-flaps documented in Year I research
spread_layout: production and graphic-culture subjects enter the magazine as primary editorial material
image: technical/graphic evidence participates in the editorial field
typography: typography treated as subject and visual material
material_production: wrapper can become an editorial plane rather than packaging only
temporal_translation: outer state can reveal an inner editorial state without behaving like ordinary navigation

issues.editorial_problem: Let real printed matter enter the magazine instead of merely being described.
spread_layout: foreign printed objects interrupt the normal page field
image: attached printed ephemera functions as evidence
typography: local typography of inserted objects is preserved
material_production: attached postcard/invitation material documented in earlier pass
temporal_translation: reveal an evidence object while preserving its independent visual system

issues.editorial_problem: Treat magazine layout itself as an explicit editorial question.
cover: jacket-with-flaps documented in Year I research
spread_layout: layout is discussed as a designed relation, not automatic symmetry
typography: hierarchy and page construction are understood as editorial decisions
temporal_translation: digital sequence should expose hierarchy through state, not decorative motion

issues.editorial_problem: Raise everyday printed matter to the level of aesthetic and civic responsibility.
spread_layout: compare bad/common graphic matter with rational redesign logic
image: ordinary tickets/forms are legitimate design evidence
typography: clarity, hierarchy and practical reading are aesthetic concerns
material_production: mass-produced everyday print is part of visual culture
temporal_translation: before/after should reveal a reasoning change, not just a cosmetic transition

issues.editorial_problem: Investigate causes and chains of visual ugliness rather than treating bad design as isolated taste failure.
sequence: diagnosis should trace causes, not merely rank examples
temporal_translation: show how one poor decision propagates through later states

issues.editorial_problem: Treat foundries and type production as the starting infrastructure of editorial design.
image: technical production evidence belongs inside design discourse
typography: typeface choice starts upstream at production culture
material_production: foundry logic is part of editorial capability
temporal_translation: surface choice should retain provenance to source capability

issues.editorial_problem: Make technical demonstration and European graphic exchange part of the magazine's cultural argument.
spread_layout: out-of-text insert breaks the normal page rhythm
image: front/back advertising-demonstration insert from ink/color manufacturer
typography: technical/commercial material can coexist with editorial content
material_production: insert is a real production specimen, not an illustration of one
sequence: cover -> pages -> out-of-text demonstration object -> return
temporal_translation: insert should arrive as a distinct state with its own rules, persist, then return without being absorbed into parent style

issues.editorial_problem: Maintain issue-specific visual invention within a stable publication identity.
cover: cover by Carlo Dradi and Attilio Rossi
image: production advertisements form part of the visual ecology
typography: publication and industrial suppliers share one editorial environment
material_production: ink/paint and Linotype producers are visibly present
sequence: editorial and production ecosystems remain adjacent
temporal_translation: supporting systems can appear as contextual layers rather than hidden metadata

issues.editorial_problem: Join practical clarity and beauty in everyday information design.
typography: most important information should receive strongest hierarchy; small schematic graphics may aid orientation
material_production: industrial material and production processes remain visible
sequence: ordinary-use problem -> hierarchy analysis -> practical graphic remedy
temporal_translation: prioritize essential information at first state; reveal secondary detail on demand without flattening hierarchy

issues.editorial_problem: Create impact typographically without decorative noise.
spread_layout: impact should come from type scale and weight rather than ornamental underlining/filler
typography: scale, weight and balanced modern type are primary expressive devices
colour is a controlled note, not decoration
temporal_translation: emphasis should come from semantic scale/state change, not animation garnish

issues.editorial_problem: Reconcile advanced reproduction technique with equally advanced taste.
spread_layout: glued out-of-text colour demonstration insert interrupts 24-page issue
image: Lorilleux colour demonstration insert signed Alfredo De Pedrini
subscriber cover examples appear inside the issue
typography: Monotype and subscriber examples coexist with criticism
material_production: glued coloured insert is both technical sample and editorial object
sequence: advertising/technical specimen -> editorial critique of coloured inserts -> further examples
temporal_translation: a generated visual should be paired with evaluation rather than accepted merely because technique succeeds

issues.editorial_problem: Close the first year by returning the wrapper itself to the editorial system.
image: advertising and production ecology remains visible through closing pages
typography: issue identity and production information coexist
material_production: book jacket with wings printed by Chiattone graphic-art workshop
sequence: outer wrapper -> issue -> production ecosystem -> outer close
temporal_translation: digital issue can have a threshold state distinct from cover and first article

year_level_findings: Aesthetic judgement is applied to ordinary information, not only prestige objects.
Technical capability is never enough: reproduction quality must be matched by contemporary taste.
The magazine is a laboratory where production methods, specimens, criticism and finished design coexist.
A stable publication identity can tolerate radical issue-level visual reinvention.
Material interruptions such as wrappers, glued inserts and out-of-text sheets are semantic devices, not decoration.
Hierarchy, scale and practical use are aesthetic questions.
Failure analysis belongs inside design training: bad design should be traced to causes, not merely rejected by taste.
next_pass: Visual pass for issues 01-06 and 08-10, then 1934 full 12-issue ledger. Promote only grammars supported by repeated issue evidence into canonical Atlas families.
